title: ED laceration documentation

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports laceration or abrasion, location, size and depth, bleeding, contamination, foreign-body concern, underlying structures, distal perfusion, dressing, splinting, tetanus, and return or disposition documentation.
user_facing_items.population: Adults and children with acute illness or injury presenting to first-contact emergency care.
user_facing_items.setting: First-contact emergency units and resource-limited emergency-care settings.
restrictions: Exact for structured trauma history, secondary survey, extremity perfusion, and open-wound assessment; partial for minor outpatient injury follow-up, imaging, closure, antibiotics, and UAE pathways.

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports signs and symptoms, allergies, medicines, past history, last intake, events or mechanism, examination, interventions, reassessment, and disposition documentation.
user_facing_items.population: Adults and children with acute illness or injury presenting to first-contact emergency care.
user_facing_items.setting: First-contact emergency units and resource-limited emergency-care settings.
restrictions: Exact for structured trauma history, secondary survey, extremity perfusion, and open-wound assessment; partial for minor outpatient injury follow-up, imaging, closure, antibiotics, and UAE pathways.
user_facing_items.rationale: The exact WHO/ICRC trauma history supports onset, mechanism, severity, associated symptoms, relevant negatives and risk context for a laceration without inferring depth, contamination or complication.

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports inspection for wounds, bruising, swelling, tenderness, deformity, range of movement, neurological findings, severe pain, and other injury signs.
